# Release verification

Keep GitHub distribution, host installation, directory submission and public directory availability separate. An uploaded draft or successful security scan does not mean the listing is live.

For each release, verify the Claude manifest and repository marketplace, the OpenAI portable directory and transport ZIP, local links, component counts and archive round-trip bytes. Compare remote release asset SHA256 digests with the verified local archives. Preserve published archive bytes; corrections require a new version.

Research review must include nested request fields and embedded credentials in URLs, not only top-level schema keys. Examples must validate against the supported plugin projection and the inspected upstream schema. A public Actor listing, input acceptance or spending approval does not establish permitted acquisition. Review the actual route's execution profile; import-only routes cannot launch from this plugin.

Directory-only fields such as the logo, support, privacy, documentation and terms links can produce Claude Code compatibility warnings. Keep them when the directory identifies them as listing fields with no action needed. Read the actual findings before changing working metadata.

Updates use a repository-scoped GitHub push webhook with JSON payloads and SSL verification. Signing secrets belong in GitHub webhook configuration, never source, release assets, examples or logs. Verify test delivery and directory receipt without retaining the secret. The webhook prompts directory scans; it does not schedule marketing tasks or bypass review.
